sources.entry: OpenOLAT - Learning management system for teaching, education, assessment and communication. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: OpenOlat is a web-based learning management system (LMS) for teaching, learning, assessment and communication, written in Java.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OpenOlat as a web-based e-learning platform with a modular toolkit for course authors offering a range of didactic options. It says each installation can be extended, adapted to organizational needs, and integrated into existing IT infrastructure. The architecture is described as aiming for low resource use, scalability and security. A REST API is available, which can be enabled in the admin panel and documented there. The README is mostly a developer guide: it covers setting up the project in Eclipse with Tomcat and PostgreSQL, alternate MySQL and Oracle databases, JavaScript/CSS compression, and running JUnit and Selenium tests. Links to user, admin and installation documentation are listed but not included in the README.
use_cases: author e-learning courses with didactic modules
manage a learning management system for an organization
integrate e-learning into existing IT infrastructure
how_to_run: Install Maven 3.8+, Git, Java 17 and Tomcat 10.0 or 10.1
Clone the repository and import it into Eclipse via Import -> Git -> Projects from Git (with smart import)
Copy olat.local.properties.sample to src/main/java/olat.local.properties and adjust it
Create the PostgreSQL user and database openolat, then load src/main/resources/database/postgresql/setupDatabase.sql
In Eclipse, select the tomcat and postgresqlunittests Maven profiles and run Maven -> Update Project
Run the project on a Tomcat 9.0 server in Eclipse and log in as administrator
notable: Modular toolkit for course authors with a wide range of didactic options
Can be integrated into existing IT infrastructure and extended per installation
Built-in REST API, documented in the admin panel
Uses Spring context configured through olat.local.properties
caveats: MySQL is supported but not recommended and support may end; Oracle support is experimental and not recommended for production
Full Selenium test run takes about 60-90 minutes and the JUnit suite about 10 minutes
The README says the community membership/partner program funds development
